atoms.text:
Act I, Scene III

(The damaged ship lays in a desert, surrounded by nothing but hot sand. It smokes, groans and hisses. A latch opens and Captain Joth, Doctor Loyt and Kozzer exit slowly and cautiously. They are wearing helmets. Kozzer is trying to take its helmet off.)

Doctor Loyt: Stop, Kozzer. We don’t know if the atmosphere is breathable yet.

(Kozzer stops fidgeting with its helmet and starts exploring its surroundings curiously.)

Captain Joth: So, what’s the plan, Loyt? This looks an awful lot like the red sandy planet. We wasted many orbits around the sun walking around looking for nothing up there.

Doctor Loyt: (following Kozzer, seemingly unconcerned) We just decide on one direction and follow it until we find anything of interest.

(Captain Joth sighs and follows reluctantly. They are shown walking, day turning to night and then turning to day again. At one point, Kozzer suddenly stops and barks. Captain Joth and Doctor Loyt look up to see what the matter is. They see cars on a highway in the distance.)

Captain Joth: (stammering) Is — Is that what I think it is?

Doctor Loyt: (whispering in awe) I think it is. We’ve found life, Joth! We are not alone in the Universe anymore! We were never alone!

instruction.text: Why do they think the cars must mean that there is life on Planet Blubber?

b: ++Cars are like spaceships. Someone must drive them which means there must be living things where cars are.
The cars give out a smelly odour.
The passing cars make sounds like fast winds.
